after.kpi_headline: Release asset fetches (mostly automated), no target; organic measured for the first time

human_gated: npm login --auth-type=web, then scripts/publish-all.sh --go. Until then npx -y @theluckystrike/mcp-<name> is E404 on every page.
Glama listing claim: the only remaining blocker on the awesome-mcp-servers PR.
Decision on the registry namespace experiment (docs/SEO_INDEXATION_R1.md addendum).
shipped: Stripe product_write human gate removed permanently: Checkout Sessions now price inline, so every current and future server gets a checkout with no dashboard step. 28 of 31 buyable ids reached Stripe before; 33 of 33 do now, including office-suite which was a bare 404.
A defect that would have taken money and withheld the licence key on every inline-priced sale, found and fixed before any sale existed.
All 114 registry manifests repointed from the robots-disallowed /buy/ redirect to the /s/ product page. Ships with the next release; the registry rejects a same-version republish.
Sitemap cut from 312 URLs to a curated set; the 216 client-by-product permutations now carry noindex,follow and stay live for users.
IndexNow set up and every sitemap URL submitted to Bing, Yandex, Seznam and Naver, accepted HTTP 200.
Organic traffic measured for the first time: Cloudflare GraphQL plus Search Console, both wired into a repeatable script.
delivery-schedule built as the 31st server, 53 tests, stdio-verified, with an id-reuse defect found and fixed.
28 new guides, and the estate-wide office-suite figures corrected to the measured 31 children and 292 tools.
KPI set corrected so crawler fetches are no longer reported as a met install target.
did_not_do: v0.21.0 release and the registry republish, which is what actually delivers the manifest fix.
Setup pages for delivery-schedule: deliberately skipped, since the same page shape was just measured as 75% duplicate and marked noindex.
The git-install fallback for npm: recipe proven and documented, not rolled out, because it force-pushes 31 mirrors and npm login supersedes it.
